topBooks: Sum: Forty Tales from the Afterlives
Symphony for the City of the Dead

books.title: Just Kids
books.author: Patti Smith
books.note: I read this on a plane ride in one sitting and was sobbing at the end. A really good breakdown of how it feels like to be when & where it's all happening- for Patti it's the whole counterculture art industry in new york (which if you know me, I love!), kind of feels like tech today in SF (at risk of sounding cliche).

books.title: If on a Winter's Night a Traveler
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.note: Calvino does it again! Extremely satisfying ending and proposes some really prescient questions on what writing and art is in the world of non-human generated words... and a really fun premise.

books.title: Symphony for the City of the Dead
books.author: M.T. Anderson
books.note: I've re-read this 10+ times and it's what made Shostakovich my favorite composer. Absolutely great, and M.T. Anderson isn't even a biographer by trade!

books.title: Invisible Cities
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.note: My foundational text, find the text+crowd-sourced annotations here: https://invisible-cities.vercel.app/. I really love this book for its puzzles and how sometimes it suddenly clicks what it can mean.

books.title: The Adventures of Kavalier & Clay
books.author: Michael Chabon
books.note: This book really takes you on a journey and you get to revel in the magic of making your own fantasy world (of comics) while constantly being reminded of the tragedies of the real world.

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
books.author: Amor Towles
books.note: Modern Russian lit- no detail is ignored, no sentence is meaningless...

books.title: Sum: Forty Tales from the Afterlives
books.author: David Eagleman
books.note: Kind of a must-read!! Hypotheses of what the afterlife is, irregardless of religion. Super short so you can read it in one sitting.

books.title: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead
books.author: Tom Stoppard
books.note: I always have a copy or two of this to hand out. A sort of fanfiction of Hamlet focused on two unlucky side characters, but I love it for the countless throwaway lines that hit you like a truck.

books.title: How Much of These Hills is Gold
books.author: C. Pam Zhang

books.title: Homegoing
books.author: Yaa Gyasi
books.note: Generations, one per chapter. Stunning structure.

books.title: Bluets
books.author: Maggie Nelson
books.note: "suppose I were to begin by saying that I had fallen in love with a color." Find my playlist for this book [here](https://open.spotify.com/playlist/6Z3O7HiOYcz19rPhHhPGH5?si=6923b5ddc0ab4139).

books.title: Sophie's World
books.author: Jostein Gaarder
books.note: One of the first books I really loved and read and to be honest I think I was too young to fully grasp it. It's kind of an overview of Western philosophy and its history + some fun plot.

books.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
books.author: Gabrielle Zevin
books.note: To me, it's a beautiful tribute to the power of friendship and what it can bring you as you stay friends your entire life. I kind of like that it's not really about romance... and I like that it feels very applicable to me :).

books.title: A Little Life
books.author: Hanya Yanagihara
books.note: Really not the overly trauma-dumping story people like to think it is. That's just not the point of the book!

books.title: Crying in H Mart
books.author: Michelle Zauner
books.note: If you're of the specific demographic this book is made for, you have to read it. Also read it in one sitting on the plane and it left me sobbing (while in the middle seat, sandwiched between two buff guys). Love your mother.

books.title: The Three-Body Problem
books.author: Cixin Liu
books.note: Obviously. (Todo: re-read + read the rest of the trilogy.)

books.title: The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
books.author: Mark Haddon

books.title: There Is No Antimemetics Division
books.author: qntm
books.note: SCP in general is a great website to read, but this book specifically is so mind-bending and increasingly becomes the sort of thing we should become comfortable thinking about.

books.title: Humble Pi
books.author: Matt Parker
books.note: Matt Parker is one of my favorite youtubers of all time and I even saw him in Edinburgh at the Fringe Fest!

books.title: Games: Agency as Art
books.author: C. Thi Nguyen
books.note: C. Thi Nguyen has a ton of great writing on the internet you should read. This book is no exception and he talks a lot about how we can think of the world as play and how we can achieve great things in the world through that lens... (very dumbed down version, you should read it).

books.title: Being Mortal
books.author: Atul Gawande
books.note: [Read in conjunction w/ Elderhood.] We should re-think end of life care, but it's always easy to say that until it becomes your own parents that you have to make decisions about.

books.title: The Sunflower
books.author: Simon Wiesenthal
books.note: Such a cool premise, where you start with a specific story from WW2 and then a series of essays from people of different religious, philosophical, and political beliefs responding to it.

books.title: I Am a Strange Loop
books.author: Douglas Hofstadter
books.note: A good argument for what consciousness is, I really like the idea of the careenium.

books.title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
books.author: Douglas Hofstadter
books.note: (Still unfinished.)

books.title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
books.author: Bill Bryson

books.title: Little Women
books.author: Louisa May Alcott
books.note: Did you know it's a trilogy? And it's actually pretty good!

books.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
books.author: Jules Verne

books.title: The Scarlet Pimpernel
books.author: Baroness Orczy
books.note: This was the actual origin of the idea of a vigilante, and the character design is shockingly similar to Batman :).

books.title: Where the Mountain Meets the Moon
books.author: Grace Lin

books.title: Crisis on Infinite Earths
books.author: Marv Wolfman
books.note: Best DC comic series.

Good Faith

albums.note: Underrated, this is a great album. Obviously HTBAHM is the best Glass Animals album but this is close too.

films.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
films.note: The one I cry to every single time

films.title: Across the Spider-Verse
films.note: The second one was better than the first... which was already one of my top 4. Soooo good.

films.title: Kinds of Kindness
films.note: Controversial but I really loved the acting and premise, a very very uncomfortable watch.

films.title: Challengers
films.note: The music! The pacing!! The tension!!!

films.title: Paprika
films.note: A movie about dream BCI and a story on what it can do to the world. I like that it's not necessarily dystopian or utopian.. it's not making such a clear cut argument in that way

films.title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
films.note: This movie inspired me to book flights to Iceland a month later. We even went to Stykkisholmur to see where they shot this movie!

films.title: Resurrection
films.note: SO GOOD. Spent the whole time watching it deeply emotional, and it was even crazier to hear the very specific dialect my mom's family spoke in this movie. M83 also made such a beautiful soundtrack (and is how I found out about this film).

films.title: Flow
films.note: Really really beautiful and totally deserved the Oscar.
